classification: single-factor substitution in the C sleeve of the R344 extended-window portfolio; intraday/overnight volatility composition

gold_proxy.rule: monthly close > 200-day MA uses gold; otherwise 50/50 treasury+dividend

hypothesis: Replacing the C sleeve generic 15% low-volatility leg with an industry-neutral 15% intraday-risk-share leg improves the 2022 weak-market tail and net-of-5x-cost breadth without materially degrading long-window return or drawdown.
limits: Open/previous-close returns use adjusted prices and can include corporate-action effects if the adjustment factor is stale.
The 20-day volatility decomposition is a statistical risk proxy, not a structural model of information flow.
Financial firms are handled by within-industry neutralization rather than separate treatment.
Current-snapshot industry classification is backfilled through history.
Membership is reconstructed and ETF qfq is not official PIT total return.
The common window starts in 2022 because TTM financial factors are unavailable earlier.
The 10% C cap, broad C design and gold trend rule were selected in prior post-hoc research.
